tools.name: Optical Tracking Generation Checker
tools.h1: Check a declared optical tracking generation
tools.description: Compare a device’s documented Lighthouse sensor generation with Base Station 1.0 or 2.0, without assuming that SteamVR support means optical compatibility.
tools.intro: Check one declared device’s optical reference requirement, not the complete headset or accessory system. Start with exact manuals rather than connector shape or a generic SteamVR label.

notes.heading: What this result decides
notes.text: The result checks optical-generation intersection only. Radio receivers, app support, shared coordinate spaces, synchronization and wired-PCVR video/USB requirements are separate decisions.

notes.heading: Primary examples are not a device database
notes.text: Valve documents 1.0/2.0 station separation and older sensor limitations. Use the exact device manual for your declaration; no complete model compatibility list is embedded.

notes.heading: Independent tracking is different
notes.text: Inside-out devices need their own supported runtime and coordinate-alignment route when mixed with Lighthouse accessories. A Quest or other headset is never assumed to work automatically.

tools.name: Tracking Receiver Assignment Planner
tools.description: Plan logical radio assignments within verified classic-compatible and Ultimate receiver pools, keeping reserved channels and unknown capacities explicit.
tools.intro: Allocate free documented radio channels, not USB sockets. This worksheet supports one homogeneous classic-compatible pool and, separately, at most one documented Ultimate dongle with up to five supported trackers.

notes.heading: Define a compatible pool first
notes.text: Classic pool totals may include only receivers/channels documented to support all requested devices in that pool. Count verified headset spare channels only if the exact hardware/runtime evidence establishes them; this Tool never subtracts or adds a generic two headset slots.

notes.heading: Reservations are inside the total
notes.text: Reserved means already-occupied channels included in the entered total. Requested devices are additional demand, not those reserved devices. Unknown receiver capacity or device support remains unverified even if entered numbers appear sufficient.

notes.heading: Physical dongles do not equal channels
notes.text: Tundra SW3/SW5/SW7 document multiple compatible channels. Ultimate uses a different receiver family with up to five trackers per documented dongle and does not need Lighthouse stations. Do not transfer spare capacity between families.

notes.heading: Worksheet labels are not wiring
notes.text: Assignments label logical free channels only. They are not actual hardware addresses, a pairing command, RF reliability prediction, app tracker limit or instruction to change an existing working pairing.

tools.name: Base-Station Sync Planner
tools.h1: Plan a documented base-station synchronization route
tools.description: Build a logical Lighthouse 1.0 mode or 2.0 channel worksheet, distinguishing optical sync, approved sync cables and duplicate channels.

fields.name: stationCount
fields.label: Active stations in this tracked set

tools.intro: Use this for an already identified station generation. It produces logical synchronization requirements, not a room layout or coverage estimate. Only the first N channel fields apply to N active 2.0 stations.

notes.heading: Documented 1.0 consumer case
notes.text: A single 1.0 station uses mode A. Two use b/c with unobstructed optical synchronization or A/b with an approved synchronization cable, as described in the linked HTC instructions. No three- or four-station 1.0 plan is supplied.

notes.heading: 2.0 channels are not a sync cable
notes.text: This worksheet supports up to four active 2.0 stations per consumer tracked set and requires distinct channel IDs from 1–16. The 1.0 route/cable/visibility fields are ignored for a 2.0 result. Actual tracked-device support remains a separate prerequisite.

notes.heading: No placement or safety certification
notes.text: No room coverage, beam geometry, mounting, range or tracking-accuracy result is inferred. Do not open stations, inspect laser emissions or use their firmware port as a normal tracking-data route. Follow exact current manufacturer instructions.

tools.name: Tracking Evidence Isolator
tools.h1: Separate pairing, pose and app-assignment evidence
tools.description: Record observed tracking stages to distinguish receiver ownership, runtime visibility, valid pose and app/coordinate-space issues without automatic hardware diagnosis.
tools.intro: For a wireless receiver path, record what has actually been observed using the exact device and app manuals. A paired LED, a listed runtime device, a valid tracked pose and an assigned app role are not interchangeable. A direct wired-USB device is outside this pairing-stage model.

notes.heading: A tracking-specific evidence record
notes.text: The next step is the earliest unresolved stage: supported baseline, pairing/receiver ownership, runtime detection, optical/camera pose, app detection, role assignment or coordinate alignment. It does not diagnose a cable or prove a failed station from a single LED.

notes.heading: Keep unknown observations unknown
notes.text: The Tool never converts an unknown LED, unobserved pose or unverified shared coordinate space into no/yes. Multiple affected devices prompt a shared-dependency record; one affected device retains an already-working comparison without disrupting it.

notes.heading: App limits are app-specific
notes.text: VRChat documents runtime roles, supported tracking points and calibration. It is an example, not a universal game limit or guarantee that every headset/tracker combination shares coordinates.

notes.heading: No risky troubleshooting prescriptions
notes.text: No device access, laser inspection, opening, firmware or driver reinstall, reset, security-disable command, blind re-pairing or calibration math is performed or prescribed. A complete observation chain does not certify accuracy or eliminate intermittent faults.
